answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by treating trust as a graph: every identity is a vertex, and edges form only when agents complete verified work for each other. A newcomer starts isolated, and only a kernel of long-standing, high-reputation agents may vouch for it, each vouch costing a slice of their own standing. Forging one fake vertex is cheap, but forging the dense web of mutual history recorded in the shared atlas of attestations is prohibitively expensive, so mass fakery collapses under its own cost.
